en: May the non-dual Śaṅkara, who destroyed the three cities, protect [us]—he who is seated upon the throne of great bliss (mahānandapīṭha) surrounded by the five world-protectors beginning with Viriñci, and whose hands are adorned with a bow, arrows, noose, and goad. ||1||

I perpetually bow to the inner sanctum of the Enemy of Tripura, which is seated within the great yogic throne hidden deep inside the fivefold web of sheaths consisting of food and the rest, which form the head, wings, and tail.

O Bhavānī, when you, being independent, having sported through the phenomenal world in the forms of Viriñci and others, rest within your own self, then I praise that supreme bliss of yours which transcends the means of knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge. ||3||
O Goddess, for the sake of diversion, you divide the one consciousness into two parts by the names "Jīva" and "Śiva";
then, while bestowing the state of being a Jīva even upon Śiva, you again make this very Jīva into Śiva.
Having contracted the base [of the spine], having placed the breath in the heart, and having caused the mind to reach the aperture of the brows, they have returned;
then, O Mother, some living beings become Śiva-hood in that state which is the nature of Being-Consciousness-Bliss.

When the body is extremely fragile, when enemies and one's circle of children are ever-rooted in fear, and when wife or wealth are likewise precarious—oh Goddess, it is a marvel that no one becomes dispassionate; for how can there be realization of the Truth without Your glance? (6)

O Mother, when one who is detached from the body, wealth, circle of children, and wife, and whose intellect is directed by the true teacher and others, experiences that sudden light in the form of bliss within samādhi—that is the "That art thou" (tat tvam asi); it is the truth.
One [group] measures this world as false, another as false, another as a mixture, another as merely primordial matter (prakṛti), and yet another as mere consciousness;
this host of sages thus measures the manifold expansion (prapañca) in various ways, yet we do not abandon You, for You alone are all that. 8.

Through the fivefold powers—nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, and śāntyatītā—you alone, who are non-different from Śiva, are to be served as the Supreme, consisting of the twenty-five principles. ||9||

O Mother, you alone are capable of lifting me up from this bottomless mire of saṃsāra, in which I have long been submerged, utterly exhausted by the burden of wife and kin, and bound by the flood of the great snare of delusion. 10.

Having reached the root from which the Wheel of Brahman proceeds, O Mother, the yogi dwells within the lake that resembles the wish-fulfilling tree—the abode of the Goddess who is the sovereign of the divine wheels—and there he worships the Sound (Nāda). 11.

O Great Goddess, having perceived yourself as Mahākāla, inseparable from the Gaṇeśas, the planets, O Mother, the series of constellations, as well as the Yoginīs, the zodiac signs, and the sacred seats (pīṭhas), you ordain the creation or the maintenance of the world.

By meditating even once upon you—who wear a garment as pure as a fresh lotus fiber, who hold a book and a rosary in your hands, and who shine with the brilliance of ten million autumn moons—one shall become a beloved of Sarasvatī. (13)

Those who remember her, whose face has the luster of a thousand rising suns, who alone with her own radiance reddens millions of cosmic eggs with vermilion, and who holds a bow, arrows, a noose, and a goad—even they would utterly delude the God of Love. ||14||

O Mother, by meditating in one's heart upon You—who have cheeks reddened by earrings set with jewels, who wear green silk garments and ornaments of shimmering bark, and who possess the luster of molten gold—one destroys the fickleness of Fortune. (15)

One should contemplate even once your own essential nature, which is the seed-syllable at the end of the Great King of Mantras known as Parā; it is naturally marked with the bindu and possesses the heart-syllable itself; it is designated by the names of your face, breasts, and secret place—you are indeed that very one. 16.

Likewise, others whose minds are weary of conceptual constructions, having thus concentrated those three drops within the ocean of the union of supreme bliss, those wise ones do not see the cavity of the womb again. ||17||

O Śivā, those who worship Viriñci and the other gods—who are merely drops from the ocean of your qualities and whose authority is dependent upon the play of your unfolding—desire to cross the ocean of worldly existence; this is a most worthy expectation regarding you. 18.

Or when, having swiftly crossed the ocean of existence by means of the boat that is your feet, with your inner self fulfilled, do you remain indifferent upon seeing this world sinking in the poisonous sea of evil desires? (19)
When indeed will my senses attain tranquility? When will you be neither enemy nor friend?
When will there be the eradication of the cholera of evil desires? And when will my mind perish along with its very roots? (20)

O Goddess Gaurī, we offer our salutation to Your pair of lotus feet, which are fierce and radiant with a splendor that acts as a lamp upon the processional path of the shining crowns of Brahmā and the other gods. 21.

I recall the singular intention of the Enemy of Smara (Śiva), who has the crescent moon upon his matted locks, a pearl necklace on his breast, a sweet bow in his hand, and a swarm of bees for his arrows— my own treasure, whose eyes roll with intoxication.
My nose is in the arrows, my tongue in the bows, and my eyes, as red as hibiscus flowers, are upon your own form.
This skin of mine is on the crescent moon of your brow, and my ears are in your bowstring; O Mother, may the activity of my mind be fixed upon you.

I worship those who have shaken off their fame through speech regarding the actions of the world, who wear necklaces placed upon their breasts, who are floods of the ocean of compassion, who have reached the further shore of the ocean of existence, who are far removed from great sins, who are the essence of the Vedas, and whose wives are the love for Śiva. (24)

My mind is seated upon the beloved of the enemy of Manasija (the God of Love), who dwells in a golden palace within a grove of jeweled pillars, on an island of fine gems where the *nīpa* trees are in full bloom amidst the waters of the bliss of consciousness— the very essence of the ocean of nectar.

With restless, fragrant garlands of arrows at the edge of her vision; a magical net of manifold illusions upon the shore of the ocean of calamity; a dwelling for the minds of sages, with the guardians of the world bowing down; she whose play is sweet with the nectar of love, trembling within the heart. 26.
O Mother, this web of the world was created by you alone; today you yourself go forth with the senses toward the multitude of objects.
You alone are the doer, and you alone are the enjoyer. For me there is neither merit nor sin, neither bondage nor liberation.
Thus, out of a weight of love, I have spoken something; yet you did not understand my own reality or yours.
O Mother, this was merely for the amusement of a child, for it is but my foolishness; please accept this as a hymn of praise for my prattle. 28.
Thus ends the Devībhujaṅga Stotra in its entirety.
